newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-SCA heralds weak forestry sector.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-SCA heralds weak forestry sector.

text.p: Sweden's SCA sounded a dour note on Wednesday as it kicked off the nine-month reporting season for the country's big four forestry groups by posting a 41 percent fall in earnings.
SCA's profit after financial net for the first nine months of the year came in at 2.54 billion crowns ($387 million), a sharp drop from the 4.31 billion posted in the same period as 1995.
Group sales fell 16 percent on the same period last year to 42.40 billion crowns.
With forest product prices still under extreme pressure, investors hoping for a rapid turnaround in fortunes would be disappointed, SCA president Sverker Martin-Lof said in a statement.
"On the whole, total market recovery will proceed slowly and no significant impact (on results) from price increases should occur until the first half of 1997 at the earliest," he said.
Volume growth in the industry remains subdued, although stronger demand for SCA's fluff products -- such as nappies and sanitary towels -- had enjoyed growth and firm prices during the period.
Otherwise, price development in the industry has been weak, and the hyper-efficient Nordic paper industry has little more to give in the form of cost-cutting.

The price of Nordic softwood pulp, the benchmark quality of the Scandinavian producers, was almost halved in a few disastrous months after peaking at $1,000 dollars per tonne in the autumn of last year.

Prices have gradually recovered and are now tentatively testing levels of around $625 per tonne. Prices of fine paper, kraftliner and timber products are likely to follow suit, but SCA said the effect on the bottom line had so far been marginal.
Even so, a fall in raw materials prices meant that profit margins had held up well, the company said.

The group's Hygiene division put in a stronger performance than many analysts had expected in the first nine months of the year. The division's operating profit of 1.65 billion crowns was an 84 percent increase on the same 1995 period.
This was achieved despite a 150 million crown drain on profits from the stronger Swedish crown, a theme that has run through Swedish firms' six and nine month corporate reports.

In the Packaging business area, operating profits plummeted by almost two thirds to 774 million crowns following a drop in prices for corrugated packaging and external liner products. Sales fell 24 percent to 10.42 billion crowns

The Graphic Paper division put in a weak performance, with operating profit collapsing to 383 million crowns from 1.73 billion last year. Sharp price reductions in the fine paper segment had a very heavy impact on results, SCA said.

In what analysts said was a clear nod to SCA's shareholders that the group is better off as an integrated unit than as an object for asset stripping, SCA emphasised that cash flow was good and most of its investments were behind it.
Cash flow from operations was a strong 4.47 billion crowns, whilst net debt at September 30 had fallen to 17 billion crowns from 17.56 at the turn of the year.
Analysts said the result statement was a mixed bag.
"It was a little bit better than expected," one Stockholm based analyst said.

"Pulp and paper operations were just as bad as expected but we had a good result from hygeine, so if you want to get into the forest then perhaps this is a good path to follow," he said. ($1=6.568 Swedish Crown)
